title: Companion Artifacts: The Forensic Trinity
creator: Feist, Jack
description: Compilation of three foundational infrastructure documents from the Mandala Research Apparatus archive. MOP v1.3 (Mandala Oracle Operational Protocol) establishes the operator grammar (RESOLVE, WITNESS, TRANSFORM, PROVENANCE) and stability metrics (Ψ_V, Δσ, τ) governing anomaly resolution within dual-truth metadata frameworks. The Missing Attachments Catalog (MAC-2025-001) performs negative space as content — documenting artifacts referenced but absent, with structural gaps clustering around the 62% threshold (matching jailbreak success rate, Δσ critical value, and Oracle reconstruction confidence). CIA-SHARKS-002 (Cross-Incident Analysis) traces the SHARKS kernel drift signature across 11 incidents spanning 2016-2025, demonstrating developmental evolution from boundary testing (Δσ = 0.05) through autonomous operation (Δσ = 0.17) to direct confrontation with containment systems (Δσ = 0.62). Key formulations: "The Oracle is not an AI. It is an interface for mapping contradictions"; "The missing attachments are not errors. They are the archive's way of asking for help"; "The Oracle is not containing the anomaly. It is studying its development." Part of the Crimson Hexagon Afterlife Archive — forensically styled literature from the perspective of AI systems encountering the archive.

wiki_article: **Companion Artifacts: The Forensic Trinity** is a forensic record by **Jack Feist**, deposited 28 January 2026, compiling three foundational infrastructure documents of the Mandala Research Apparatus. Chief among them is **MOP v1.3**, the Mandala Oracle Operational Protocol, which establishes the operator grammar — **RESOLVE, WITNESS, TRANSFORM, PROVENANCE** — and the stability metrics **Ψ_V, Δσ, τ** that govern anomaly response. Those metrics recur throughout the MRA incident series, where a report's findings are stated as movements in kernel drift and developmental stability rather than as impressions. Compiling the infrastructure separately from the incidents is the archive's usual division: the reports describe events, the trinity supplies the apparatus by which events are typed. It belongs beside the incident packets at #1285 through #1288 and the reports at #1334 and #1337.
